response.consequence: A failing delete leaves a runaway non-daemon thread that keeps hitting the server and can stall the test JVM. In the normal path, the last read can fail without being detected.
response.explanation: The test starts a non-daemon reader thread that loops until `deletedAll` is set. `deletedAll.set(true)` runs only after the delete loop completes, and it isn't in a `finally`. If a `remove()` call throws, `deletedAll` stays false and the thread keeps issuing admin requests indefinitely. The thread is also never joined. After `deletedAll.set(true)`, the thread may still be in the middle of a `groups()` call, so an exception from that last in-flight read can be added to `caughtExceptions` after `assertThat` has already run. That makes the check racy and able to miss failures.
